As I read it, .git protection stops the VM from changing hooks, and --clone leaves the hook behind since a clone doesn't copy hooks. However, the hook is still in the folder on the host. Does devvm inspect and warn when a folder already has hooks before you start?

gregwebs · Nov 6, 2026

This looks quite similar to docker sandbox (sbx). It uses Lima for VMs under the hood. Windows advertised as not supported (Lima is missing features on Windows).

Like Docker Sandbox this meets what I think should be our standards in the AI age: kernel isolation and secret shielding in addition to network and disk isolation.

I have been working on a similar project because I haven't seen one before that to me didn't have security design deficiencies. This project looks to have made good design decisions around security.

The things that are design choices for these tools are

  * agent integration
  * docker image composition
  * are vms more persistent or throw away
  * managing configuration
It does look like it has some design decisions that are optimal for convenience but might lead to inflexibility. It assumes 1 VM per directory. It is trying to auto-detect what someone needs in an image and provide well integrated images and tools out of the box but I don't see how to just provide my own image.

I think the auto detection is interesting, but tbh with my solution I've been happy with just install all the tools regardless of what a specific project needs - with a COW base layer this is cheap.

mnahkies · Nov 6, 2026

One thing I'm struggling with at the moment which I may as well ask here.

Many of my projects use pnpm, which ideally uses hard links from a shared store of dependencies.

One of my goals is to reduce the disk overhead of VM based isolation, so I'd like a shared pnpm store across projects (and the same for maven, etc as well)

With https://virtio-fs.gitlab.io/ mounts, each mount inside the VM is a separate FS, and I can't hard link across them. I've tried playing around with ideas like bind mounting the directory structure from the host in a folder to have a single virtio-fs mount inside the VM - but the bind mounts still can't be hard linked across it seems.

I'm basically wondering if I'm missing something or just trying to do something that isn't possible.

All the host folders are on the same FS - but I don't want to organise the host system around the VM mounting needs, and I also don't want to mount extraneous directories into the VM (eg: simple solution could be just mount ~/projects but kinda self defeating)

(Fedora workstation host)

zenoprax · Nov 7, 2026

I usually commit outside the sandbox. Agents will see the git history and will emulate that but they can't sign the commits. If I authorize a series of commits I can just `git rebase -i HEAD~N` and adjust the messages and re-sign at the same time. With git hooks as a threat vector I'm considering just giving them read-only access to `.git` otherwise I can't safely go back in there without the sandbox.

I don't give it access to GH - it can read most things via API or web scraping fast enough and I manually run the commands I need outside the sandbox.

No need for SSH - it's running locally.

---

Given how many holes you're poking into the container I think you'd be better served with a real VM.
